primitives.name: Residualized EPA Equivalence
primitives.verbatim_quote: # Decisive test: the EPA residual is raw EPA in disguise (r = 1.000) The whole point of residualisation is to change the ordering — to strip situational advantage out of team quality.
primitives.assumptions: Linear regression of EPA on situational variables yields negligible variance reduction; residual ordering matches raw EPA.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When basis functions lack sufficient explanatory power to shift relative team rankings.

layer2.mapping: The residual transformation is isomorphic to identity under current modeling assumptions, preserving raw EPA rank order.
layer2.telemetry: Pearson correlation coefficient r=1.000 between raw and residual EPA means.

primitives.name: Contextual Adjustment Failure
primitives.verbatim_quote: To actually change an ordering you need a basis with real situational bite: score-state × time interaction (garbage time), opponent quality, personnel, and down-distance interaction terms.
primitives.assumptions: Current basis (down, distance, field position) insufficiently captures dynamic game states affecting outcome.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Insufficient degrees of freedom in linear model to capture complex interactions.

layer2.mapping: Kernel of adjustment fails to produce meaningful perturbations in team rank due to low signal-to-noise ratio.
layer2.telemetry: Linear model has 4 degrees of freedom against 1.41 SD of noise.

primitives.name: Ordering Stability
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Why the earlier models looked like they were doing something They were reporting a *stable ordering*, and the ordering is stable precisely because it is raw EPA.
primitives.assumptions: Stable rank ordering implies that adjustments do not meaningfully alter comparative team performance metrics.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When model adjustments are decorrelated from actual performance variation.

layer2.mapping: Stable ordering reflects isomorphism between adjusted and unadjusted team quality measures.
layer2.telemetry: Consistent identical rankings across multiple models due to shared underlying metric.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core assertion is that residualizing EPA via linear regression on situational variables does not meaningfully alter team rankings. This occurs because the basis used—down, distance, field position—lacks sufficient complexity to generate substantial variation in residuals compared to raw EPA. As shown in the data, Pearson correlation is 1.000 and Spearman 0.999, indicating near-perfect preservation of rank order. The failure mode lies in the limited degrees of freedom (4) versus the inherent noise level (~1.41 SD), which precludes any meaningful discrimination between teams. Thus, while residualization aims to strip situational advantage, it instead preserves the original EPA ranking structure. This reveals a duality: the transformed metric behaves identically to the original under these constraints, making it a display-only operation rather than a selection criterion. The implications extend beyond simple ranking to broader questions of model interpretability and utility in dynamic environments where true situational effects may be masked by oversimplified modeling assumptions.
